## Featured project: GTM Engine (VERIFIABLE)

- Repo: https://github.com/layllabs/GTM-Engine (MIT, Python 3.11+, stdlib only)
- Run: `git clone https://github.com/layllabs/GTM-Engine && cd GTM-Engine && python -m gtm run`
- Expected: 28 signals to 23 accounts; tiers A8/B8/C3/DQ4; 52 drafts, 0 lint failures; 1 domain flagged for retirement
- What it does: discover events (permits, filings, ownership change, owner posts) -> dedupe across sources -> score against configurable ICPs with written reasons -> route to email/call/visit via a JSON rule table -> render and lint copy -> classify replies rules-first with schema-bound model fallback -> deliverability health with pause/retire thresholds and z-tested A/B verdicts
- Verified by: 38 tests, 28-case labeled reply eval, template lint across 38 combinations, config schema validation, em-dash check, full run; all in CI on Python 3.11/3.12/3.13
- Notable: a test parses the Mermaid lifecycle diagram and fails if it drifts from gtm/lifecycle.py
- Not public: discovery scrapers, email verifier, sequencer and CRM integrations, LLM client (employer-tied). Same schemas as production.
- Ran against live prospects: STATED

## Internal tools, prior employer (all STATED, not public)

- Email Reputation Center: one view of every sending domain and mailbox (warmup, bounce, complaints, placement, rotation). Claimed: replaced a paid monitoring tool; thresholds reused in GTM Engine.
- Orchestration layer: n8n and Gumloop workflows syncing CRM, sequencer, enrichment. Claimed: removed a daily manual sync.
- Outbound Center: manager dashboard (activity by rep, pipeline created, reply and meeting rate by sequence, pace mid-week). Claimed: used by a team of about 20 in 1:1s.
- Forecasting tool, VP dashboard, internal CRM. Origin of the shadow-CRM pattern (ADR 002).
- Aggregate claim: about $120K replaced vendor spend. STATED.

python -m gtm eval-replies                   # 28/28
python -m gtm run
python -m gtm statement                      # statement review on the sample
